conflicts.topic: which identity document a non-EU newcomer needs to get online banking codes (strong identification)
conflicts.aQuote: Banks in Finland require a foreigner’s identity card issued by the Finnish authorities to enable non-EU nationals use online banking credentials for strong identification
conflicts.bQuote: Tarvitset mukaasi voimassa olevan S-Pankin hyväksymän henkilöllisyystodistuksen ja oleskeluluvan
conflicts.note: International House Helsinki says banks require a Finnish foreigner’s identity card for non-EU nationals; S-Pankki says you need an ID document it accepts plus a residence permit, without naming the foreigner’s ID card.
conflicts.whatToDo: Treat International House Helsinki, an official source, as the safer guide, but S-Pankki sets its own rules for its own customers. Before your appointment, ask your chosen bank which documents it accepts for online banking codes, and bring your passport, residence permit and any Finnish ID card you already have.

sources.title: ihhelsinki.fi
highlights: Banks in Finland require a foreigner’s identity card issued by the Finnish authorities to enable non-EU nationals use online banking credentials for strong identification
A visit to the selected bank is required
The processing time varies between banks and when first appointment times are available

sources.title: suomi.fi
highlights: However, e-services require a tool that enables you to use strong identification online

sources.title: poppankki.fi
highlights: To be granted a strong electronic means of identification, you must have a Finnish personal identity code and be entered in the Population Information System

sources.title: nordea.fi
highlights: You can obtain online banking credentials and a strong electronic ID when you become a customer, provided you have a valid identity document required for this purpose

sources.title: s-pankki.fi
highlights: Tarvitset mukaasi voimassa olevan S-Pankin hyväksymän henkilöllisyystodistuksen ja oleskeluluvan

sources.title: nordicexpat.com
highlights: Expect a wait of a few days to a week

sources.title: hyy.fi
highlights: Due to the small number of available times for meetings in English, opening an account takes a long time
International students from outside EU/EEA countries, for instance, have been required to have a Finnish ID card in order to receive online banking IDs

sources.title: relocateineurope.com
highlights: The requirements for online banking credentials are stricter than for the account, so some newcomers leave the branch with an account and no codes

sources.title: nordicexpat.com
highlights: Done in this order, you avoid the most common failure mode: assuming the account and the codes arrive together, and being stuck unable to log in to public services for weeks

sources.title: nordicexpat.com
highlights: Nordea describes a workaround used in Finland: you can visit a police station, where your identity is verified so the electronic identification service can be activated
